text:
The Kings have 12 points from 17 games, and almost nothing about how they've played explains it. Our numbers have them at a -13 goal difference on +3.1 expected goals, with goaltending (9.4 goals allowed above expected) and finishing doing most of the damage. Even in a three-game losing streak in which they were outscored 13-4, they took 57% of the expected goals. That is why our simulations still give them a 30% playoff chance.

There is help, and there is a hole. Kevin Fiala made his season debut Thursday after a long recovery from a leg injury and picked up a power-play assist; he is one assist from 300. Artemi Panarin is out for personal reasons (ESPN estimates Nov 17), so Quinton Byfield, two points from 200, figures to take on more. Byfield is one of our sleepers: 51% for a point, above his season pace of 43%, because his line creates 4.01 expected goals per 60. Anton Forsberg is confirmed in goal.

Calgary's week has been about what it lost. Kevin Bahl is done for the season, the most written-about Flame by far, while Zayne Parekh's rise as a power-play star has filled the rest of the headlines. Dustin Wolf, confirmed, has struggled: .869 and 6.6 goals worse than expected. The Flames are 2-2-1 in their last five but with only 44% of the chances, and they sit at a 10% playoff chance. Matt Coronato is one goal from 50.

Our other sleeper is 41-year-old Corey Perry, who plays fourth-line minutes but has 3.7 expected goals in his last ten games, better than 99% of depth forwards, with eight shots from high-danger spots. We have him at 19% to score and 31% for a point. Sleepers are for information and entertainment, and they are graded publicly on our Track record page.
headline: The Kings keep outplaying their record
